text:
### 2.11 Installing an operating system

Motherboard settings and hardware options vary. The setup procedures presented in this  chapter are for reference only. Refer to  operating system documentation for  detailed information.

#### 2.11.1 Windows 7 and USB 3.0 driver for 100 Series

Based on the chipset specification, the 100 series requires USB 3.0 drivers to be preloaded  in order to use USB keyboard/mouse during  Windows 7 installation. This section is a guide  on preloading USB 3.0 drivers and installing  Windows 7.

##### Method 1: Using SATA ODD & USB devices

Load USB 3.0 drivers using the  support DVD and install  Windows 7 using a USB  device.

**Requirement:**
- 1 x  support DVD
- 1 x  Windows 7 installation source
- 1 x SATA ODD
- 1 x USB device (ODD or storage)

The USB storage device requires 8 GB or more capacity. It is recommended to format the  storage device before use.

1.  Insert the  Windows 7 installation DVD into a USB ODD, or copy all files on the  Windows 7 installation DVD to a USB storage device on a working system.
2.  Connect the USB ODD or USB storage device to your 100 series platform.
3.  Insert the  support DVD into a SATA ODD on your 100 series platform.

4.  Power on your system and press F8 during POST (Power-On Self Test) to enter the  boot screen.

5.  Select the USB ODD or USB storage device as the boot device.<PIC:Manual25_87>
{{image description: A BIOS boot device selection dialog on a grey background. It says Please select boot device, with instructions for Enter to select and ESC to boot using defaults. Options include ASUS optical drive, hard drive, ADATA USB flash drive highlighted, UEFI ADATA USB flash drive, and UEFI ASUS DVD, with OK and Cancel buttons.}}

6.  The USB 3.0 driver will be loaded automatically during installation startup.<PIC:Manual25_88>
{{image description: A Windows setup screen with a blue background and centered text reading Setup is starting...}}

The "Setup is starting..." screen will show up if the USB 3.0 driver is loaded correctly.
7.  Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the Windows 7 installation.

##### Method 2: Using a modified 7 ISO

Load USB 3.0 drivers and install  Windows 7 using a modified  Windows 7 installation DVD.

**Requirement:**
- 1 x support DVD
- 1 x  Windows 7 installation source
- 1 x Working system (PC or notebook)
- 1 x SATA ODD

1.  On your working system, create an ISO image file of the  Windows 7 installation  source using a third-party ISO software.
2.  Copy both "AutoUnattend.xml" and "AutoUnattend" folder from the root directory of  the  supporting DVD to your system.
3.  Edit the ISO file and add both "AutoUnattend.xml" and "AutoUnattend" folder into the  ISO file.
4.  Burn this ISO file onto an empty DVD to create a modified  Windows 7 installation  DVD.
5.  Insert the modified  Windows 7 installation DVD into an ODD on your 100 series  platform.
6.  Power on your system and press F8 during POST (Power-On Self Test) to enter the  boot screen.
7.  Select the ODD as the boot device.
8.  The USB 3.0 driver will be loaded automatically during installation startup.

notice:
<PIC:Manual25_89>
{{image description: A small pen or stylus-like icon centered on a blank white area.}}

The "Setup is starting..." screen will show up if the USB 3.0 driver is loaded correctly.
9.  Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the  Windows 7 installation.
##### Method 3: Using EZ Installer

Use the EZ Installer to create a modified  Windows 7 installation source.

**Requirement:**
- 1 x support DVD
- 1 x  Windows 7 installation DVD
- 1 x Working system (PC or notebook)
- 1 x SATA ODD
- 1 x USB storage device (8 GB or more)

1.  Insert the  Windows 7 installation DVD.
2.  Launch the EZ Installer located on the  support DVD.
3.  Select a method of creating a modified Windows 7 installation file:
- Windows 7 OS disk to USB storage device  - Select  Windows 7 OS disk to USB storage device  then click  Next.<PIC:Manual25_90>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer window. It explains creating a copy of a Windows 7 installation file into a USB storage device or optical disc. A dropdown says Windows 7 OS disc to USB storage device, a note warns that an 8 GB or larger USB device will be formatted, and a Next button is visible.}}

- Check  I agree  and then click  Next.<PIC:Manual25_91>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer end user license agreement screen. It shows EULA text in a scrollable box, an I agree checkbox, and Back and Next buttons.}}

- Select the source of the Windows 7 installation disk then click  Next.<PIC:Manual25_92>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer Step 1 of 3, Select your disc source. A dropdown shows an optical drive source and capacity 3181 MB, with Back and Next buttons.}}

- Select the USB storage device and click  next.<PIC:Manual25_93>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer Step 2 of 3, Insert a USB storage device. It asks for an 8 GB or larger USB storage device that will be formatted, shows a drive selection with capacity about 7519 MB, and has Back and Next buttons plus a refresh icon.}}

Click the refresh icon  if the USB storage device is not displayed.
- Click  Yes  to clear the contents on the USB storage device and create a  bootable USB device.
- Make sure to backup contents on the USB storage device, as it will be formatted.
- Once completed, click  OK  to finish.

- Windows 7 OS disk to ISO file<PIC:Manual25_94>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer window for creating a Windows 7 installation file to an ISO file. The dropdown reads Windows 7 OS disc to ISO file and a Next button is at the bottom right.}}

- Select  Windows 7 OS disk to ISO file  then click  Next.
- Check  I agree  and then click  Next.<PIC:Manual25_95>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer EULA screen for the ISO-file workflow, with license text, an I agree checkbox, Back button, and Next button.}}

- Select the source of the Windows 7 installation disk then click Next.<PIC:Manual25_96>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer Step 1 of 3 for selecting the Windows 7 installation disc source, showing an optical drive source, capacity 3181 MB, and Back and Next buttons.}}

- Select the folder to save the modified  Windows 7 installation ISO file and click  Next.<PIC:Manual25_97>
{{image description: ASUS EZ Installer Step 2 of 3, Select the destination folder for the ISO file. A text field shows D:\ and there is a Browse button plus Back and Next buttons.}}

- Once completed, click OK to finish.
- Burn this ISO file onto an empty DVD to create a modified  Windows 7  installation DVD.
4.  Insert the modified  Windows 7 installation DVD into an ODD or connect the USB  storage device with modified  Windows 7 installation files onto your 100 series  platform.
5.  Power on your system and press F8 during POST (Power-On Self Test) to enter the  boot screen.
6.  Select the ODD or USB storage device as the boot device.
7.  The USB 3.0 driver will be loaded automatically during installation startup.

The "Setup is starting..." screen will show up if the USB 3.0 driver is loaded correctly.
8.  Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the Windows 7 installation.

text:
#### 2.11.1 Windows 7 and USB 3.0 driver for 100 Series

Based on the chipset specification, the 100 series requires USB 3.0 drivers to be preloaded  in order to use USB keyboard/mouse during  Windows 7 installation. This section is a guide  on preloading USB 3.0 drivers and installing  Windows 7.

##### Method 1: Using SATA ODD & USB devices

Load USB 3.0 drivers using the  support DVD and install  Windows 7 using a USB  device.

**Requirement:**
- 1 x  support DVD
- 1 x  Windows 7 installation source
- 1 x SATA ODD
- 1 x USB device (ODD or storage)

The USB storage device requires 8 GB or more capacity. It is recommended to format the  storage device before use.

1.  Insert the  Windows 7 installation DVD into a USB ODD, or copy all files on the  Windows 7 installation DVD to a USB storage device on a working system.
2.  Connect the USB ODD or USB storage device to your 100 series platform.
3.  Insert the  support DVD into a SATA ODD on your 100 series platform.

4.  Power on your system and press F8 during POST (Power-On Self Test) to enter the  boot screen.

5.  Select the USB ODD or USB storage device as the boot device.<PIC:Manual25_87>
{{image description: A BIOS boot device selection dialog on a grey background. It says Please select boot device, with instructions for Enter to select and ESC to boot using defaults. Options include ASUS optical drive, hard drive, ADATA USB flash drive highlighted, UEFI ADATA USB flash drive, and UEFI ASUS DVD, with OK and Cancel buttons.}}

6.  The USB 3.0 driver will be loaded automatically during installation startup.<PIC:Manual25_88>
{{image description: A Windows setup screen with a blue background and centered text reading Setup is starting...}}

The "Setup is starting..." screen will show up if the USB 3.0 driver is loaded correctly.
7.  Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the Windows 7 installation.

##### Method 2: Using a modified 7 ISO

Load USB 3.0 drivers and install  Windows 7 using a modified  Windows 7 installation DVD.

**Requirement:**
- 1 x support DVD
- 1 x  Windows 7 installation source
- 1 x Working system (PC or notebook)
- 1 x SATA ODD

1.  On your working system, create an ISO image file of the  Windows 7 installation  source using a third-party ISO software.
2.  Copy both "AutoUnattend.xml" and "AutoUnattend" folder from the root directory of  the  supporting DVD to your system.
3.  Edit the ISO file and add both "AutoUnattend.xml" and "AutoUnattend" folder into the  ISO file.
4.  Burn this ISO file onto an empty DVD to create a modified  Windows 7 installation  DVD.
5.  Insert the modified  Windows 7 installation DVD into an ODD on your 100 series  platform.
6.  Power on your system and press F8 during POST (Power-On Self Test) to enter the  boot screen.
7.  Select the ODD as the boot device.
8.  The USB 3.0 driver will be loaded automatically during installation startup.

- Connect the equipment to an outlet on a circuit different from that to which the receiver  is connected.

LAN port LED diagram showing Activity/Link LED and Speed LED positions above the RJ-45 port.

Motherboard diagram locating the TPM header at the lower edge of an ASUS Z170 PRO GAMING board. A pinout labeled TPM shows PIN 1 and signals including F_CLKRUN, F_SERIRQ, F_FRAME#, F_LAD3 to F_LAD0, S_PCIRST#, C_PCICLK, +3VSB, +3V, GND, and GND.

Motherboard fan connector diagram with callouts A through F. It marks CPU_FAN, CPU_OPT, CHA_FAN3, CHA_FAN1, CHA_FAN2, and EXT_FAN headers, with pin labels such as fan PWM, fan IN, fan PWR, GND, +5V, and extension fan sensor pins.

Motherboard ATX power connector diagram. Callout A points to EATX12V with +12V and GND pins; callout B points to EATXPWR with labeled rails including +3 Volts, +5 Volts, +12 Volts, GND, Power OK, Standby Power, PSON#, and PIN 1.

Motherboard thermal sensor connector diagram. A note says the thermistor cable is purchased separately. The board callout points to T_SENSOR1, a 2-pin header labeled SENSOR IN and GND with PIN 1 shown.

Motherboard front panel audio connector diagram labeled AAFP. It compares an HD-audio-compliant pin definition with AGND, NC, SENSE1_RETUR, SENSE2_RETUR, PORT1L, PORT1R, PORT2R, SENSE_SEND, and PORT2L against a legacy AC97 compliant definition with AGND, NC, MIC2, MICPWR, Line out_R, NC, NC, and Line out_L.
Motherboard diagram locating the ROG_EXT connector along the lower edge of the board. The enlarged header is labeled ROG_EXT and shown as two adjacent rows of pins.

Motherboard USB 3.0 connector diagram. The board callout points to USB3_12, with a 20-pin header pinout labeled USB3+5V, IntA_P1_SSRX-/SSRX+, IntA_P2_SSRX-/SSRX+, GND, IntA_P1_SSTX-/SSTX+, IntA_P2_SSTX-/SSTX+, IntA_P1_D-/D+, IntA_P2_D-/D+, and PIN 1.
Small note-style icon showing a pen or feather on an otherwise blank white page; no readable technical text is visible.

Motherboard SATA connector diagram with callouts A and B. It locates SATA6G_1, SATA6G_2, SATA6G_3, SATA6G_4, SATA6G_5, SATA6G_6, and SATAEXPRESS connectors, with pin labels such as GND, RSATA_TXP/TXN, RSATA_RXP/RXN, Floating, Device_Reset, and Detection.

Illustration of connecting SATA cables. Green arrows show cable plugs entering a drive and motherboard SATA ports. A note says to connect the right-angle side of the SATA signal cable to the SATA device, and that the right-angle side may also connect to the onboard SATA port to avoid conflict with huge graphics cards.

Motherboard system panel connector diagram labeled PANEL. The enlarged header shows groups for +PWR_LED-, PWR_SW, SPEAKER, +HDD_LED-, RESET, and +PWR_LED-, with pin labels including PLED+, PLED-, PWRBTN#, GND, +5V, Speaker, HDD_LED+, HDD_LED-, Ground, RSTCON#, NC, and PLED-.
Motherboard diagram locating an M.2 connector at the lower-right area of the board. The enlarged connector is labeled M.2(SOCKET3) and is drawn as a long edge socket.

Motherboard USB 2.0 connector diagram. It locates headers USB78, USB910, and USB1112 at the lower edge and shows pinouts with USB+5V, USB_P7-/P7+, USB_P8-/P8+, USB_P9-/P9+, USB_P10-/P10+, USB_P11-/P11+, USB_P12-/P12+, GND, NC, and PIN 1.
Small warning icon on a mostly blank page, shown as a triangular sign with a lightning bolt inside. No other readable text is present.
Motherboard standby power LED diagram. The board callout points to SB_PWR, with indicator states shown as a red circle labeled ON Standby Power and an empty circle labeled OFF Powered Off.
Motherboard model name LED diagram. The board callout highlights the illuminated area near the ASUS Z170 PRO GAMING logo, with a row of small red LED rectangles labeled Model name LED.
Table describing model name LED lit modes. Breathing mode: The LEDs blink intermittently. Still mode: The LEDs become solid red.
Motherboard diagram with a red highlighted LED trace running along the left and lower edges of the board, indicating the decorative lighting path on the PCB.
Table describing LED lit modes. Breathing mode: The LED blinks intermittently. Flowing mode: The LED lights up and dims like flowing water. Still mode: The LED becomes solid red.

ASUS Z170 PRO GAMING motherboard support CD interface. The left sidebar has Driver, Utilities, Manual, and Special icons; the main driver list includes items such as Intel Chipset Driver, Google Chrome Browser, Google Toolbar, Intel LAN Driver, Realtek Audio Driver, and Norton Internet Security. A button labeled Install is highlighted with the note Click to install.

ASUS EZ Update screen with callouts. It shows a dark update utility, a Check Now button for automatic update, a field and Browse button to find and select the BIOS from file, a boot logo selection area, and an update action for updating the BIOS.

EZ Flash Update window asking Please choose a way to update your BIOS. Two large options are shown: by USB with a red USB icon and by Internet with a globe icon, plus a Next button at the lower right.

Blue BIOS boot-device selection screen. It instructs using up and down to move selection, ENTER to select boot device, and ESC to boot using defaults. Listed choices include P2: ST3808110AS (76319MB), aigo miniking (250MB), UEFI:(FAT) ASUS DRW-2014L1T(4458MB), P1: ASUS DRW-2014L1T(4458MB), UEFI:(FAT) aigo miniking (250MB), and Enter Setup.

ASUSTeK BIOS Updater for DOS screen. It shows current ROM information for board Z170 PRO GAMING, an update ROM box with unknown fields, a PATH field set to C:\, a drives panel with C: and D:, and a files panel listing Z17PG.CAP with size and date. Footer shortcuts include Enter Select or Load, Tab Switch, V Drive Info, arrow keys Move, Esc Exit.
Red BIOS confirmation dialog reading Are you sure you want to update the BIOS? The Yes button is highlighted in green and No appears to the right.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility EZ Mode screen with red callouts identifying panels and controls. It shows system information, CPU temperature and voltage, SATA information, fan profiles, EZ System Tuning, boot priority, QFan Control, default settings, Advanced Mode (F7), Search on FAQs, and boot device priority.
Small note-style icon showing a pen or feather on an otherwise blank white page; no readable technical text is visible.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode screen with red callouts. It labels the menu bar, MyFavorite, Q-Fan control, EZ Tuning Wizard, Quick Note, Hot Keys, menu items, sub-menu item, general help, configuration fields, scroll bar, popup window, last modified settings, EZ Mode shortcut, and a hardware monitor sidebar.

Green table explaining BIOS menu bar tabs. My Favorites saves frequently used settings and configuration; Main changes basic system configuration; Ai Tweaker changes overclocking settings; Advanced changes advanced system settings; Monitor displays system temperature, power status, and fan settings; Boot changes system boot configuration; Tool configures special functions; Exit selects exit options and loads default settings.

ASUS Q-Fan Control screen with callouts. It shows fan selection for CPU FAN, CHA1 FAN, CHA2 FAN, CHA3 FAN, EXT FAN1, EXT FAN2, and EXT FAN3, buttons for Optimize All, PWM, DC, profile choices Standard, Silent, Turbo, Full Speed, and Manual, and buttons Undo, Apply, and Exit (ESC).

Q-Fan Control manual configuration screen. A fan curve graph is highlighted with speed points, PWM and DC mode buttons appear above, fan choices are listed at left, and controls include Manual, Fan off, Undo, Apply, and Exit (ESC). A callout says to click to manually configure your fans.

ASUS EZ Tuning Wizard screen in Advanced Mode. Tabs OC and RAID are shown, with RAID selected. A left step list includes Current System Configuration, PC scenario, Main cooling system, and Estimation tuning result. The right panel shows Current System Configuration with CPU frequency 2600 MHz, ratio 26x, BCLK 100.0 MHz, temperature 38 degrees C, and DRAM frequency 4096 MB (DDR4 2133MHz). Buttons Next and Cancel appear.

RAID Setup Wizard storage configuration screen. The left step list shows Enable RAID mode and Storage Configuration. The main panel says Welcome to the EZ RAID Setup Wizard and lists available storage disk drives including two ST3808110AS ports, each 74.5GB. Next is disabled and Cancel is available.

Storage Function Selection screen in the RAID wizard. It asks which function to use for the storage disk drive and shows selectable icons for Easy Backup and Super Speed, with Back, Next, and Cancel buttons.

Storage Function Selection screen asking to select the RAID type for the selected storage function. Easy Backup (RAID1) is highlighted in yellow, while Easy Backup (RAID10) is greyed. Back, Next, and Cancel buttons are shown.

Storage Function Selection screen asking to select the RAID type for the selected storage function. Super Speed (RAID0) is highlighted in yellow, while Super Speed (RAID5) is greyed. Back, Next, and Cancel buttons are shown.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode, My Favorites tab. The left menu lists CPU Core Ratio, DRAM Frequency, CPU Core/Cache Voltage, DRAM Voltage, SATA Configuration, Onboard Devices Configuration, CPU C States, Fast Boot, Next Boot after AC Power Loss, Boot Logo Display, and POST Delay Time. A hardware monitor sidebar shows CPU and memory status.

Instructional BIOS image showing steps to add favorites. Text says press F3 or click (F3)MyFavorite to open the Setup Tree Map screen, then select BIOS items to save. The screenshot labels Main menu panel, Submenu panel, and Selected items shortcut.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode, Main tab. The BIOS Information panel lists BIOS Version 0215 x64, Build Date 06/11/2015, EC1 Version MBEC-GMB-0102, and processor and memory details. System Language is set to English, with hardware monitor data at right.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode, Ai Tweaker tab. The screen lists target CPU and DRAM frequencies at top, then settings such as AI Overclock Tuner, ASUS MultiCore Enhancement, CPU Core Ratio, BCLK Frequency : DRAM Frequency Ratio, DRAM Odd Ratio Mode, DRAM Frequency, OC Tuner, and EPU Power Saving Mode with dropdown fields.
A standalone triangular warning icon with an exclamation mark on a mostly blank page.
A triangular warning icon above a small pen or stylus-like graphic on an otherwise blank page.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility in Advanced Mode. The Advanced tab is selected and CPU Configuration is highlighted in a left menu that also includes Platform Misc Configuration, System Agent Configuration, PCH-IO Configuration, SATA Configuration, USB Configuration, Onboard Devices Configuration, APM Configuration, and Network Stack Configuration. A hardware monitor panel appears on the right.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode on the Monitor tab. A list of temperature and fan readings is visible, including CPU Temperature, MotherBoard Temperature, VRM Temperature, PCH Temperature, T_Sensor Temperature, external sensor temperatures, CPU Fan Speed, and optional fan speeds, with a hardware monitor sidebar.

ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode on the Boot tab. Boot Configuration options are shown, including Fast Boot enabled, Next Boot after AC Power Loss, Boot Logo Display, POST Delay Time, Boot up NumLock State, Above 4G MMIO BIOS assignment, Wait for F1 if Error, Option ROM Messages, Interrupt 19 Capture, and Setup Mode.
ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode on the Tool tab. Menu items include ASUS EZ Flash 3 Utility, Setup Animator set to Disabled, ASUS Overclocking Profile, and ASUS SPD Information.
ASUS UEFI BIOS Utility Advanced Mode on the Exit tab. Options include Load Optimized Defaults, Save Changes and Reset, Discard Changes and Exit, and Launch EFI Shell from USB drives.

A BIOS boot device selection dialog on a grey background. It says Please select boot device, with instructions for Enter to select and ESC to boot using defaults. Options include ASUS optical drive, hard drive, ADATA USB flash drive highlighted, UEFI ADATA USB flash drive, and UEFI ASUS DVD, with OK and Cancel buttons.
A Windows setup screen with a blue background and centered text reading Setup is starting...
A small pen or stylus-like icon centered on a blank white area.

ASUS EZ Installer window. It explains creating a copy of a Windows 7 installation file into a USB storage device or optical disc. A dropdown says Windows 7 OS disc to USB storage device, a note warns that an 8 GB or larger USB device will be formatted, and a Next button is visible.
ASUS EZ Installer end user license agreement screen. It shows EULA text in a scrollable box, an I agree checkbox, and Back and Next buttons.
ASUS EZ Installer Step 1 of 3, Select your disc source. A dropdown shows an optical drive source and capacity 3181 MB, with Back and Next buttons.

ASUS EZ Installer Step 2 of 3, Insert a USB storage device. It asks for an 8 GB or larger USB storage device that will be formatted, shows a drive selection with capacity about 7519 MB, and has Back and Next buttons plus a refresh icon.
ASUS EZ Installer window for creating a Windows 7 installation file to an ISO file. The dropdown reads Windows 7 OS disc to ISO file and a Next button is at the bottom right.
ASUS EZ Installer EULA screen for the ISO-file workflow, with license text, an I agree checkbox, Back button, and Next button.
ASUS EZ Installer Step 1 of 3 for selecting the Windows 7 installation disc source, showing an optical drive source, capacity 3181 MB, and Back and Next buttons.
ASUS EZ Installer Step 2 of 3, Select the destination folder for the ISO file. A text field shows D:\ and there is a Browse button plus Back and Next buttons.
A standalone triangular warning icon with a lightning bolt in the center on a mostly blank page.
